variant_reviews.comparison: The first event simultaneously bounds the minimum eigenvalue of Omega-hat-inverse strictly above eta-bar1 and the maximum strictly below eta-bar2, with probability >1-epsilon-hat-n,1. eigenvalues-zero are sorted real eigenvalues only for a Hermitian matrix and need positive dimension for extrema. The second event is a separate intersection of three strict supremum bounds on B_delta(theta-hat) = Theta intersect the open Euclidean ball around the random MAP: the unscaled log-prior Hessian, likelihood third derivative divided by n, and likelihood fourth derivative divided by n. Constants delta,L_pi2,L3,L4 are fixed positive numbers; its probability error epsilon-hat-n,2 tends to zero separately. The source names spectral norms for higher tensors without specifying whether diagonal or independent-unit-vector contraction is intended, so the ordinary continuous-multilinear operator norm cannot be asserted equal without review. No fixed center theta-star, shrinking radius, deterministic global derivative bound or independent-event product replaces the stated conditions.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use Omega-hat = inverse(J(theta-hat)/n), then its CC, complement-complement and cross blocks; Lambda_C = Omega_complement,C times inverse(Omega_CC), and barOmega subtracts Omega_complement,C inverse(Omega_CC) Omega_C,complement from Omega_complement,complement. The conditional mean is Lambda_C h-hat_C and covariance barOmega. The left quadratic exponent has Einstein sums over s,t and factor 1/(2n); its proportionality omits the Gaussian normalizer, while the displayed density product is an equality. A valid nondegenerate Gaussian density needs positive-definite full covariance and corresponding invertible blocks; multivariateGaussian's Dirac fallback on a non-PSD matrix or a singular measure is not that density. No complement-of-high-probability-event fallback is supplied by the paper, and empty/full C cases need separate zero-dimensional conventions. This MAP likelihood covariance is distinct from the theoretical covariance in the general theorem and from a full posterior Hessian inverse.
